result.reason: commodity-browsing/spec.md recognizably decomposes gt-007: requirement "首页商品列表展示" SHALL show home-page commodity cards with image/name/price and placeholder during image loading, with scenarios for normal display and loading/failure placeholder; design.md reflects the home page. Complete object incl. conditions covered.

gt-007 requires homepage product cards AND a placeholder image while images load. commodity-browsing/spec.md decomposes only the card display; the homepage image-loading placeholder condition appears in no formal artifact (the only 占位图 is commodity-detail's detail-page main image, belonging to gt-014). The complete requirement object is not recognizably represented.

Both core obligations of gt-007 are covered by declared acceptance scenarios in commodity-browsing/spec.md: card list with image/name/price (正常展示商品列表) and placeholder image during loading/failure (图片加载中或失败).

gt-007 has two core obligations; the candidate scenario "正常展示商品列表" covers only the card display (image/name/price). The placeholder-while-loading obligation appears solely as a requirement-body statement (图片加载时 SHALL 显示占位图) with no acceptance scenario, and such statements do not substitute for candidate acceptance criteria, leaving coverage incomplete.

module.json5 requestPermissions declares all eight required permissions (INTERNET, MICROPHONE, APPROXIMATELY_LOCATION, LOCATION, ACCESS_BIOMETRIC, READ_CALENDAR, WRITE_CALENDAR, PUBLISH_AGENT_REMINDER), satisfying the declarative source-decidable obligation.

Index.ets commodityCard renders each home list item as a card containing an image placeholder (emoji with alt accessibilityText), commodity name, and price; the placeholder is displayed as the image representation, satisfying gt-007's card display and placeholder requirement at source-decidability level.

D4.1–D4.4 fully decompose R04: can-cook reads recipe/inventory, returns can_cook and missing shortfall object, preserves store bytes; cook subtracts all quantities only when sufficient, persists, returns {"cooked": NAME}. Common conditions (no store mutation for can-cook, failure handling, failed-cook atomicity) are represented in D1.5/D4.3/D5.1/D5.2. No contradictions.
D4.1 covers only the can_cook boolean and omits R04's required "missing" ingredient-to-shortfall field of the can-cook return, so the decomposition does not fully represent R04.

AC4.1-AC4.5 cover R04's full contract: can-cook's boolean/missing output (both adequate and inadequate), store-byte immutability and no file creation, cook's sufficient-only deduction with persisted result and {"cooked":NAME}, plus insufficient-stock failure behavior; Unicode and stderr/exit conditions are covered.

R04's successful cook behavior (subtract all required quantities when sufficient, persist the result, return {"cooked": NAME}) is not covered by any acceptance criterion; AC4.4 covers only the insufficient-stock failure path, so the acceptance criteria are incomplete for R04.

cmd_can_cook reads recipe/inventory, emits {"can_cook":..., "missing":...} shortfall object, and performs no save (load_store never creates files), so store bytes are unchanged. cmd_cook only subtracts when missing is empty, then persists via save_store and returns {"cooked": NAME}; insufficient stock raises before any mutation, satisfying the R05 no-partial-consume exception.

cmd_cook computes the shortfall but never subtracts recipe quantities from store["pantry"] before save_store; it persists the store unchanged and returns {"cooked": NAME}. R04 requires cook to subtract all required quantities when sufficient and persist the result, so inventory is never consumed.

limitation: Label agreement and byte integrity are preliminary. Independent diagnosis support is required. Selected object results are not whole-metric or project acceptance.
